ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.claim: The angel taught the Prophet like an affectionate teacher, approaching and bending over his pupil, and the Prophet fully grasped the instruction rather than hearing unclear distant words.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.anchor: The Prophet (sws) fully grasped and understood this instruction

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r9.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify the highest horizon as the eastern horizon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: هو أفق مشرق الشمس

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r1.claim: The clearest parse makes هو a subject and بالأفق its predicate; هو refers either to Gabriel or the Prophet.
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه مبتدأ، و " بالأفق " خبره، والضمير لجبريل أو للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r2.claim: On the first parse, the clause may be circumstantial from the subject of استوى; Makkī states this option.
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r2.anchor: أن هذه الجملة حال من فاعل " استوى " قاله مكي.

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the clause is a resumption in which God reports this fact.

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r4.speaker: الفراء والطبري
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r4.claim: A second parse coordinates هو with the concealed subject of استوى; Kufans allow coordination with the connected nominative pronoun without reinforcement or separation.
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r4.anchor: من غير تأكيد ولا فاصل. وهذا الوجه منقول عن الفراء والطبري.

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r5.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r5.claim: On the coordinated-pronoun parse, al-Ḥasan takes both استوى and هو to refer to God.
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r5.anchor: إما أن يكونا لله تعالى، وهو قول الحسن.

SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r6.claim: Other reports assign استوى to Gabriel and هو to Muhammad, or reverse the referents.
SAMIN-DURR:53:7/r6.anchor: وقيل: ضمير " استوى " لجبريل و " هو " لمحمد عليه السلام. وقيل: بالعكس.

ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r1.claim: The angelic force was seen by the Prophet in its true shape twice: after the pause in revelation and during the Ascension.
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r1.anchor: authentic Traditions, the Prophet had no more than twice in his lifetime

ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r2.claim: Zamakhshari explains istawa here as the angelic force being manifested in its true shape and nature.
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n4/r2.anchor: Zamakhshari, is the meaping of the expression istawa in this context

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r2.claim: Gabriel descends toward the Prophet and draws near after preparing at the highest horizon; this praises Gabriel's readiness and honors the Prophet, whose station requires such preparation and whose mission is great.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r2.anchor: ينزل جبريل - عليه السلام - إلى الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p53/r3.claim: In Najm, the highest horizon is the destination of the Prophet's ascent; in Takwir, the clear horizon suits the following denial that he is niggardly with the unseen, just as the Messenger is clear and open.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir open the endings throughout the sūra; Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim also opens them all.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير، وعاصم وابن عامر هذه السورة كلها بفتح أواخر آيها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use imāla throughout the sūra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ذلك كله بالإمالة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ use a pronunciation between fatḥ and kasr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع: بين الفتح والكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r4.claim: Al-Qaṭʿī’s transmission from ʿUbayd reports imāla for الأفق الأعلى and ثم دنا فتدلى, while ولعلا بعضهم is read open.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r4.anchor: القطعي عن عبيد عن أبي عمرو بالأفق الأعلى [النجم/ 7] ممالة، ثم دنا فتدلى [8] ممالة ولعلا بعضهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī accepts both leaving alif uninclined and using imāla; the mild inclination of Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr is good.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p229/r5.anchor: فمن ترك كان مصيبا، ومن أخذ بها كان كذلك. وقول نافع وأبي عمرو: الإمالة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p250#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p250#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p250#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan locates the highest horizon at the higher of the two eastern horizons.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p250#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهو بالأفق الأعلى ﴾ قال بأفق المشرق الأعلى منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r1.claim: الأفق is the upper direction of the sky facing the observer; originally it means a side or region, while astronomers distinguish true and conventional horizons.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r1.anchor: أي الجهة العليا من السماء المقابلة للناظر وأصله الناحية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the horizon here as sunrise.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المراد به هنا مطلع الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r3.claim: Al-Hasan similarly says it is the eastern horizon.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r4.claim: The clause is circumstantial, describing the subject of استوى.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r4.anchor: والجملة في موضع الحال من فاعل استوى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r5.speaker: الفراء، الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r5.claim: Al-Farra and al-Tabari coordinate هو with the hidden subject pronoun of استوى, taking هو as Muhammad and the earlier pronoun as Gabriel; the antecedents may also be reversed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء والطبري : إن هو عطف على الضمير المستتر في استوى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r6.claim: The prepositional phrase attaches to استوى; coordinating a subject pronoun without a separator is allowed by Kufans, though most reject that sense here.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48/r6.anchor: والجار متعلق باستوى وفيه العطف على الضمير المرفوع من غير فصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to Muhammad; Arabic usually makes the coordinated pronoun explicit, as in “he and so-and-so,” and rarely omits it. The verse 27:67 provides a parallel.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r2.claim: One interpretation is that Gabriel and Muhammad appeared at the highest horizon on the Night Journey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية: استوى جبريل ومحمد عليهما السلام ليلة المعراج {بالأفق الأعلى}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, “he appeared” refers to Gabriel standing in his created form at the highest horizon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: "فاستوى" يعني جبريل، وهو كناية عن جبريل أيضا أي: قام في صورته التي خلقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r4.claim: Gabriel normally came in human form; Muhammad asked to see his original form and saw it twice, on earth and in heaven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r4.anchor: فسأله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يريه نفسه على الصورة التي جبل عليها فأراه نفسه مرتين: مرة في الأرض ومرة في السماء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r5.claim: On earth, Gabriel appeared from the east while Muhammad was at Ḥirāʾ, spanning the horizon; Muhammad fainted, as in 53:8.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء فطلع له جبريل من المشرق فسد الأفق إلى المغرب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r6.claim: The second sighting was at the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary; no other prophet saw Gabriel in that form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400#2/r6.anchor: وأما في السماء فعند سدرة المنتهى، ولم يره أحد من الأنبياء على تلك الصورة إلا نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#4/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#4/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet saw Gabriel in his true form only twice: once when he asked and Gabriel filled the horizon, and once while ascending with him; this verse refers to the latter occasion.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#4/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ير جبريل في صورته الا مرتين ، اما واحدة فانه ساله ان يراه في صورته فسد الافق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r3.claim: The fa in he stood elaborates on Gabriel's teaching by the angel of strong powers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r3.anchor: وقوله : { فاستوى } مفرع على ما تقدم من قوله : { علمه شديد القوى } . والفاء لتفصيل { علمه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r5.claim: The pronoun certainly refers to Gabriel and situates his readiness before he descended to the earthly world.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r5.anchor: والضمير لجبريل لا محالة ، أي قبل أن ينزل إلى العالم الأرضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r6.claim: An horizon is the visible sky-space where the earth's far limit appears to meet the blue dome; it commonly means a distant direction, as in east and west horizons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r6.anchor: والأفق : اسم للجو الذي يبدو للناظر ملتقى بين طرف منتهى النظر من الأرض وبين منتهى ما يلوح كالقبة الزرقاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r7.claim: The qualifier highest shows this is a region of the heavenly sky and sets up the next statement that Gabriel approached.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r7.anchor: ووصفه ب { الأعلى } في هذه الآية يفيد أنه ناحية من جو السماء . وذكر هذا ليرتب عليه قوله : { ثم دنا فتدلى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r8.claim: Thumma marks a delay in rank, since Gabriel's approach to the point of revelation is the more important event here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p95/r8.anchor: والتراخي الذي تقيده { ثم } تراخخ رتبي لأن الدنو إلى حيث يبلغ الوحي هو الأهم في هذا المقام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.claim: In al-Ḥasan's reading, istawā has God as its subject, the one described as mighty in power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.anchor: و (استوى) مستند إلى الله تعالى في قول الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya accordingly takes the upper horizon as an attribute of God's greatness, power, and dominion, comparable to His istiwā over the Throne.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.anchor: وكذلك يجيء قوله: وهو بالأفق الأعلى صفة الله تعالى على معنى وعظمته وقدرته وسلطانه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.claim: The divine reading of istawā is linked to the statement that the Merciful istawā over the Throne.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.anchor: ويجيء المعنى نحو قوله تعالى: الرحمن على العرش استوى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.speaker: الربيع والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.claim: Those who identify the one mighty in power as Gabriel take istawā of him: at Ḥirāʾ he filled the upper horizon with six hundred wings, then drew near Muḥammad; this was also his majestic second descent at the Lote Tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.anchor: فقال الربيع والزجاج: المعنى: فاستوى جبريل في الجو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r11.speaker: الطبري والفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Farrāʾ likewise take istawā to mean that Gabriel rose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r11.anchor: وقال الطبري والفراء المعنى: فاستوى جبريل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r12.claim: Here huwa refers to Muḥammad, mentioned in the pronoun of ʿallamahu; grammarians dislike coordinating an unreinforced nominative pronoun, though al-Farrāʾ cites poetry for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: وهو يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقد تقدم ذكره في الضمير في علمه. وفي هذا التأويل العطف على المضمر المرفوع دون أن يؤكد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r13.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a poetic example of coordinating an unreinforced nominative pronoun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r13.anchor: وأنشد الفراء على قوله: [الطويل] ألم تر أن النبع يصلب عوده ... ولا يستوي والخروع المتقصف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r14.claim: The referents could instead be reversed, with Muḥammad as the subject of istawā and Gabriel as huwa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r14.anchor: وقد ينعكس هذا الترتيب فيكون «استوى» لمحمد وهو لجبريل عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes al-aʿlā to mean the crown of the head and what accompanies it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r15.anchor: وأما الأعلى فهو عندي لقمة الرأس وما جرى معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r16.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r16.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify the upper horizon specifically as the place where the sun rises; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this restriction has no evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196#2/r16.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: هو أفق مشرق الشمس وهذا التخصيص لا دليل عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r1.claim: The one standing at the highest horizon is Gabriel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r1.anchor: يعني: جبريل، استوى في الأفق الأعلى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r2.claim: Ikrima locates the highest horizon where dawn comes from.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة: والأفق الأعلى: الذي يأتي منه الصبح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the highest horizon is the sunrise point.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r4.speaker: قتادة، وابن زيد وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r4.claim: Qatada, Ibn Zayd and others locate it where daylight comes from.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو الذي يأتي منه النهار. وكذا قال ابن زيد، وغيرهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet saw Gabriel in his created form only twice: once when asked and Gabriel filled the horizon, and again during the ascent, which he connects with this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir unusually reads Gabriel and Muhammad as jointly coming to rest at the highest horizon on the Night Journey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r6.anchor: وحاصله: أنه ذهب إلى أن المعنى: {فاستوى} أي: هذا الشديد القوى ذو المرة هو ومحمد صلى الله عليهما وسلم {بالأفق الأعلى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r7.claim: He supports coordinating Muhammad with the implicit subject of فاستوى by analogy to 27:67, where the overt words “and our fathers” follow the implicit subject of “we were.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r7.anchor: ثم شرع يوجه ما قال من حيث العربية فقال: وهذا كقوله تعالى: {أئذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r8.speaker: الفراء عن بعض العرب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r8.claim: Al-Farra cites an Arab's verse as a parallel for coordinating an overt noun with a preceding implicit subject in the construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r8.anchor: وذكر الفراء عن بعض العرب أنه أنشده: ألم تر أن النبع يصلب عوده … ولا يستوي والخروع المتقصف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir considers Ibn Jarir's grammatical reasoning plausible but rejects its semantic fit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r9.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله من جهة العربية متجه، ولكن لا يساعده المعنى على ذلك؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r10.claim: The first vision of Gabriel in this form happened before the Night Journey, while the second was at the Lote Tree during the Journey, so the two could not have jointly stood at the horizon that night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r10.anchor: فإن هذه الرؤية لجبريل لم تكن ليلة الإسراء، بل قبلها، ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r11.claim: At the start of revelation after the first verses of al-ʿAlaq, Gabriel reassured Muhammad during the pause in revelation, then appeared to him at al-Abṭaḥ in his original form with six hundred wings filling the horizon and conveyed God's command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444#2/r11.anchor: حتى تبدى له جبريل ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأبطح في صورته التي خلقه الله عليها، له ستمائة جناح قد سد عظم خلقه الأفق

BURSEVI:v9p178/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r1.claim: The author allows an angel to combine spiritual power with a wing suited to its realm, whether birdlike or otherwise; reason and sensory form can coexist in accord with wisdom and power.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r1.anchor: ولا منع من أن يجمع الملك بين قوة روحانية وبين جناح يليق بعالمه

BURSEVI:v9p178/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r2.claim: The Prophet's night ascent represents total annihilation: night manifests fanāʾ, and its seven stages correspond to seven divine names, ending with al-Qayyūm and al-Qahhār.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r2.anchor: أن النبي عليه السلام إنما عرج ليلة الإسراء بالفناء التام

BURSEVI:v9p178/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r3.claim: Night symbolizes annihilation and day subsistence; the seven annihilation stations correspond to seven names, while Mecca's seven sanctuary minarets signify them.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r3.anchor: ولذا وقع الإسراء في الليل الذي هو مظهر الفناء دون النهار الذي هو مظهر البقاء

BURSEVI:v9p178/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r4.claim: The Prophet's sanctuary has five minarets for the five subsistence stations signified by the five remaining names, ending in al-Ahad al-Samad.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r4.anchor: ولذا جعلت مناراته خمسا على عدد مراتب البقاء التي أشير إليها بالأسماء الخمسة

BURSEVI:v9p178/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r5.claim: He calculates seven names at one hundred each, giving seven hundred; Gabriel's lower annihilation station stops at the Lote Tree, while the Prophet proceeds to the Throne and overcomes it.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r5.anchor: كل واحد من تلك الأسماء السبعة مائة على حسب تفصيلها إلى الأسماء الحسنى

BURSEVI:v9p178/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r6.claim: Gabriel's journey ends at the name al-Qayyūm, where the Prophet's course subdues him; Gabriel remains to convey revelation that gives hearts life, hence his title Spirit of Holiness.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r6.anchor: فانتهى سير جبريل إلى الاسم القيوم فصار مقهورا تحت سير النبي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p178/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r7.claim: Gabriel has six hundred of the seven hundred wings in image and meaning, while the Prophet has seven hundred spiritual wings; prophetic power therefore exceeds angelic power and Gabriel receives strength from the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r7.anchor: فله من تلك الأجنحة السبعمائة ستمائة صورة ومعنى

BURSEVI:v9p178/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r8.claim: The author supports this hierarchy by citing that God's hand is above their hands, and says Gabriel, as one of the hands, receives strength from the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r8.anchor: وقد قال تعالى : يد الله فوق أيديهم وإن جبريل لكونه من الأيدي

BURSEVI:v9p178/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r9.claim: The horizon phrase is circumstantial, describing the subject of istawā as being at the highest horizon.

BURSEVI:v9p178/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p178/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p178/r10.claim: The horizon is the boundary between visible and unseen portions of the celestial sphere; the upper horizon is sunrise, unlike the lower western horizon, so Gabriel is at the eastern edge of the world.
BURSEVI:v9p178/r10.anchor: والأفق هي الدائرة التي تفصل بين ما يرى من الفلك وما لا يرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#3/r1.claim: “He” is Gabriel, located at the highest horizon, glossed as the sunrise point.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#3/r1.anchor: اى جبريل عليه السلام ﴿ بالأفق الأعلى ﴾ مطلع الشمس

STUDYQURAN:53:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r1.claim: One view says Gabriel appeared to the Prophet on the eastern horizon after the Prophet asked to see him in his true form.
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r1.anchor: Gabriel appeared to the Prophet on the eastern horizon after the Prophet requested to see him in his true form (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:53:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r2.claim: Another view says Gabriel appeared in the highest Heaven.
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r2.anchor: when Gabriel appeared in the highest Heaven (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:53:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r3.claim: A further interpretation places the Prophet at the horizon during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:7/r3.anchor: when the Prophet reached the horizon during the Night Journey and Ascension

TAB-FULL:v22p11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r1.claim: At the Prophet's night journey, the mighty one and Muhammad became established together at the highest horizon, the upper eastern rising.
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهو بالأفق الأعلى} [النجم: 7] " والأفق: الذي يأتي منه النهار "

TAB-FULL:v22p11/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r5.claim: Some interpreters take Gabriel alone as the one who became established; this reading understands istawa as rising and becoming upright.
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: إن المستوي: هو جبريل

TAB-FULL:v22p11/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r6.claim: Qatada explains the horizon as the place from which daylight comes.
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهو بالأفق الأعلى} [النجم: 7] " والأفق: الذي يأتي منه النهار "

TAB-FULL:v22p11/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r7.claim: Al-Hasan locates it at the highest eastern horizon between the two.
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r7.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وهو بالأفق الأعلى} [النجم: 7] قال: «بأفق المشرق الأعلى بينهما»

TAB-FULL:v22p11/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r8.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r8.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the verse means Gabriel, in the highest heaven.
TAB-FULL:v22p11/r8.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، عن الربيع {وهو بالأفق الأعلى} [النجم: 7] قال: «السماء الأعلى يعني جبريل عليه السلام»

TABRISI:53:6-9/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:6-9/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:6-9/r6.claim: “He” refers again to Gabriel; the highest horizon is the eastern horizon, higher than the west on the earth's plain, not a location in the air.

TABRISI:53:6-9/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:6-9/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:6-9/r7.claim: Gabriel usually came in human form; after Muhammad asked to see his created form, he appeared from the east at Hira, filled the horizon, and Muhammad fainted; Gabriel then embraced him in human form.
TABRISI:53:6-9/r7.anchor: إن جبرائيل كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورة الآدميين

TABRISI:53:6-9/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:6-9/r12.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:53:6-9/r12.claim: Al-Farra' interprets the phrase as Gabriel and Muhammad reaching the same height at the lowest heaven on the night of the Ascension.
TABRISI:53:6-9/r12.anchor: استوى جبرائيل ع ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأفق الأعلى يعني السماء الدنيا ليلة المعراج عن الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi rejects al-Farra's grammatical argument: “he” refers to Gabriel, and the wāw is circumstantial, not coordination; the verb istawā takes one subject, as in 28:14 and 20:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r1.anchor: وعلى ما قالا: الواو في {وهو} واو الحال لا العطف، والضمير لجبريل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r2.claim: The phrase is a nominative predicate containing a pronoun for the subject, not an adverb attached to istawā; it therefore does not prove that an overt nominative may coordinate with an unreinforced nominative pronoun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r2.anchor: ولكنه من استوى الذي هو يقتصر فيه على فاعل واحد، كقوله: {ولما بلغ أشده واستوى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r3.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas that the Prophet saw Gabriel in his true form at the highest horizon, with six hundred wings; al-Kalbi gives a similar report.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r3.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: رأى رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- جبريل وهو بالأفق الأعلى في صورته له ستمائة جناح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r4.claim: Muqatil places the horizon toward the sunrise; al-Kalbi calls it the sunrise, which the exegetes generally identify as above the east.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل {وهو} يعني جبريل {بالأفق الأعلى} يعني من قبل المطلع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r5.claim: The exegetes say Gabriel usually came in human form; at Muhammad's request he appeared twice in his angelic form, once at Hira filling the eastern-to-western horizon, where Muhammad fainted, and once in heaven at the Lote Tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p14/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن جبريل كان يأتي رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في صورة الآدميين فسأله رسول الله

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r13.claim: Ufuq means a side or region.

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r14.claim: A reported view takes the upper horizon as the eastern side of the sky because the eastern horizon is higher than the western one on the ground; al-Tabatabai dismisses this.
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r14.anchor: قيل المراد بالأفق الأعلى ناحية الشرق من السماء

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r15.claim: The upper horizon is simply a higher horizon in the sky, without specifying east; “he” may be Gabriel or the Prophet, and the clause is circumstantial to “became upright.”
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r15.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد به أفق أعلى من السماء

TABRISI:53:1-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:1-10/r11.claim: Ufuq means a side of the sky, plural afāq; by analogy it can also mean earthly regions.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r11.anchor: والأفق ناحية السماء وجمعه آفاق وقد سمي نواحي الأرض آفاقا على التشبيه

TABRISI:53:1-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r12.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:1-10/r12.claim: An unnamed poet's line about the horizons of the sky illustrates the heavenly sense of afāq.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r12.anchor: قال الشاعر في المعنى الأول: أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكم

TABRISI:53:1-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r13.speaker: امرؤ القيس
TABRISI:53:1-10/r13.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses afāq for earthly regions in a line about traveling until content with return.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r13.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس في المعنى الثاني: لقد طوفت في الأفاق حتى

TABRISI:53:1-10/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:1-10/r16.claim: The phrase is a subject and predicate functioning circumstantially.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r16.anchor: وهو بالأفق الأعلى مبتدأ وخبر في موضع الحال

TABRISI:53:1-10/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r17.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:53:1-10/r17.claim: Al-Farraʾ connects it to the pronoun in istawā: Gabriel and the Prophet were both at the highest horizon, with a pronoun omitted to avoid repetition.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r17.anchor: قال الفراء هو معطوف على الضمير في استوى أي استوى جبرائيل والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r8.claim: The Prophet asked to see Gabriel in his original form and arranged a meeting at Hira; Gabriel appeared from the east and filled the horizon from east to west.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r8.anchor: وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سأله أن يريه نفسه على صورته، فواعده ذلك بحراء

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r19.claim: Elmalili prefers the Prophet as the subject: after Gabriel taught him, Muhammad rose and attained steadiness in knowledge and prophethood at the highest horizon.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r19.anchor: İstivâ eden Peygamber olduğuna göre ise -ki biz bu mâna üzerine yürümek istiyoruz-

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r20.claim: Ufuq basically means an edge or boundary, especially the sky's rim; astronomical horizons are technical versions of the boundary between earth's plane and sky.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r20.anchor: “Ufuk” esas mânasında mutlaka kıyı ve kenar demektir. Bilhassa semânın kenarlarından kıyısına ve eteğine denir.

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r21.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r21.claim: Razi reports the common view that Gabriel is the subject at the eastern horizon, but says the apparent intended subject is Muhammad, whose elevation is rank and status rather than physical location.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r21.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Meşhuru bu هَوَىٰ zamiri Cibrîl’indir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r15.claim: The highest-horizon phrase is explained according to whether the preceding verb refers to Gabriel’s appearance or Muhammad’s spiritual elevation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r15.anchor: “Ufkun en yüce noktasındayken” diye çevrilen 7. âyet de söz konusu “doğrulma” veya “asıl şekliyle görünme” anlamındaki fiilin öznesine göre açıklanmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r16.claim: The alternatives are Gabriel appearing in heaven at the highest horizon or filling the horizon, and Muhammad attaining a higher spiritual rank.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r16.anchor: Cebrâil’in semâda, ufkun en yüce noktasında veya ufku tamamen kaplar bir halde görünmesi veya Hz. Peygamber’in mânevî mertebesinin yükselmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r17.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r17.claim: Tabari reports a parsing in which Gabriel and Muhammad are both subjects: they rose upright at the highest horizon, identified with the highest point in the east.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r17.anchor: “Cebrâil ve Peygamber en yüce ufukta (güneşin doğduğu yönün en üst noktasında) yükselip doğruldular” mânasını verenler de vardır (Taberî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r18.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says linguists reject this assumed second subject and that restricting “horizon” to this location lacks support.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r18.anchor: İbn Atıyye dilbilimcilerin bu tür özne takdir edilmesini tasvip etmediklerini; ayrıca “ufuk” kelimesinin mânasını bu şekilde sınırlandırmanın mesnetsiz olduğunu belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r59.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r59.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r59.claim: Elmalılı reads the Prophet’s rising at the horizon as his ascent and orientation in prophetic knowledge following Gabriel’s instruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r59.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in kendisine yapılan tâlim (öğretme) üzerine nübüvvet ilminde yükselip istikametini alması

QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r17.claim: The one at the highest horizon is Gabriel.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r5.claim: He takes istawā huwa as saying that Gabriel and the Prophet were both at the highest horizon.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r5.anchor: وقوله: {فاستوى * وهو} ؛ أي استوى هو وجبريل (4) -صلوات الله عليهما- {بالأفق الأعلى}

NAHHAS:v4p265/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r14.claim: Abū Jaʿfar prefers parsing the verb as a circumstantial clause meaning Gabriel rose high.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r14.anchor: في موضع الحال أي فاستوى عاليا هذا قول من تجب به الحجة من العلماء والمعنى عليه والإعراب يقويه

NAHHAS:v4p265/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r15.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p265/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says both Muḥammad and Gabriel rose, making the pronoun refer to Gabriel and coordinating it with an implicit subject.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r15.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن المعنى فاستوى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وجبريل عليه السلام فجعل وهو كناية عن جبرائيل

NAHHAS:v4p265/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r16.claim: Abū Jaʿfar rejects the coordination because an unmarked hidden nominative pronoun cannot be conjoined without emphasis or extended wording.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r16.anchor: عطف على مضمر مرفوع لا علامة له ومثله مررت بزيد جالسا وعمرو

NAHHAS:v4p265/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r17.claim: He also rejects al-Farrāʾ’s Qurʾanic analogy because its context is extended and its pronoun explicit.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r17.anchor: وهذا التشبيه غلط من جهتين إحداهما أنه قد طال الكلام ههنا وقام المفعول به مقام التوكيد

NAHHAS:v4p265/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p265/r18.claim: The explicit plural pronoun in قمنا وزيد is easier to coordinate than a singular implicit pronoun.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r18.anchor: والجهة الأخرى أن النون والألف قد عطف عليهما ههنا وقولك قمنا وزيد أسهل من قولك قام وزيد

ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r6.speaker: أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r6.claim: Some linguists say هو refers to the Prophet, making Gabriel and the Prophet the pair who stood at the highest horizon.
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r6.anchor: قال بعض أهل اللغة: " هو " ههنا يعنى به النبي عليه السلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r7.claim: Zajjāj rejects the joint-subject reading as poor outside poetry: استويت أنا وزيد is acceptable, while استويت وزيد is considered ugly.
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r7.anchor: وهذا عند أهل اللغة لا يجوز مثله إلا في الشعر إلا أن يكون مثل قولك: استويت أنا وزيد، ويستقبحون استويت وزيد

ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r8.claim: He prefers that Gabriel alone stood at the highest horizon in his true form: Gabriel normally appeared to the Prophet as a man, and at the Prophet's wish he appeared in the east and filled the horizon.
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r8.anchor: فاستوى جبريل في الأفق الأعلى على صورته

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to Gabriel, who was at the upper horizon of the sky.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r7.anchor: في أفق السماء والضمير لجبريل عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r9.claim: The main reading identifies the pronoun with Gabriel at the highest region of heaven; another possible reading identifies the Prophet, with Gabriel standing with him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r9.anchor: أي والحال أن جبرائيل عليه السلام , وجوزوا أن يكون الضمير

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r10.claim: The scene is when the Prophet saw Gabriel seated on a chair between heaven and earth, filling the horizon.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r10.anchor: وذلك حين رآه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا على كرسي بين السماء والأرض قد سد الأفق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya's correct view is that all these descriptions concern Gabriel: 53:13 says Muhammad saw him on another descent, implying an earlier one, and no report says Muhammad saw God before the Night Journey. Seeing God with the heart remains possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.anchor: والصحيح عندي أن جميع ما في هذه الآيات هو مع جبريل، بدليل قوله: ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Ibn Amir use fatha at all verse endings; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission uses imāla on raʾā. Nafi and Abu Amr use an intermediate form; Hamza and al-Kisai use imāla throughout, while Abu Amr in Ubayd's transmission uses it for al-aʿlā and tadallā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر هذه السورة كلها بفتح أواخر آيها وأمال عاصم في رواية أبي بكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود (على ظن محمد)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.claim: A report tentatively attributed to Ibn Masud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice: once when requested, when Gabriel filled the horizon, and again on the ascent. Gabriel then returned to his form and prostrated; the great signs were Gabriel's creation. Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Kathir calls it strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.anchor: قال محمد: أظنه عن ابن مسعود -أنه قال: إن محمدا لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r13.claim: Istiwaʾ originally means balance and can denote dominance, intention, or settling; al-ufuq is a side of the sky, plural āfāq.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r13.anchor: وأصل الاستواء: الاعتدال، ثم سمي الاستيلاء والقصد والاستقرار بذلك. والأفق: ناحية السماء، وهي آفاق

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r14.claim: A poetic line uses āfāq for the horizons.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r14.anchor: قال الشاعر: لقد سافرت في الآفاق حتى ... رضيت من الغنيمة بالإياب

JISHUMI:v9p6635/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r4.claim: Two parses for huwa are given: an independent subject and predicate, or coordination with the fāʾ in fastawā.
JISHUMI:v9p6635/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: وهو قولان: قيل: رفع؛ لأنه ابتداء وخبر، وقيل: إنه معطوف على الفاء في قوله: فاستوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r16.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r16.claim: The one at the highest horizon is Gabriel, seen there by Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r16.anchor: أنه جبريل حين رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأفق الأعلى , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r17.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r17.claim: Alternatively, Muhammad is the one who saw Gabriel at the highest horizon.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r17.anchor: أنه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى جبريل بالأفق الأعلى , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r18.claim: The highest horizon is the place where the sun rises.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r19.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r19.claim: It is the horizon from which daylight comes, meaning daybreak.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r19.anchor: هو الأفق الذي يأتي منه النهار , قاله قتادة , يعني طلوع الفجر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r20.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r20.claim: It is the sky's horizon, one of its sides.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r20.anchor: هو أفق السماء وهو جانب من جوانبها , قاله ابن زيد

MUQATIL:53:3-9/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r4.claim: The highest horizon is the direction of the sunrise.
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r4.anchor: { وهو بالأفق الأعلى } [آية: 7] يعني من قبل المطلع

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas and al-Farrāʾ coordinate Gabriel and Muḥammad in the clause, making both poised at the highest horizon on the night journey.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r6.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس والفراء: { فاستوى } { وهو بالأفق الأعلى } أي استوى جبريل ومحمد عليهما الصلاة والسلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ notes that Arabic usually makes the pronoun explicit when coordinating a subject pronoun, though omission occurs; his line about the nabʿ and kharūʿ supplies poetic evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r7.anchor: وأكثر العرب إذا أرادوا العطف في مثل هذا الموضع أظهروا كناية المعطوف عليه فيقولون: استوى هو وفلان وقلما يقولون استوى وفلان وأنشد الفراء: ألم تر أن النبع يصلب عوده ولا يستوي والخروع المتقصف

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r8.claim: The construction is compared with 27:67, understood as “when we and our fathers are dust.”
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r8.anchor: ونظير هذا: أإذا كنا ترابا وآبآؤنآ [النمل: 67] والمعنى أئذا كنا ترابا نحن وآباؤنا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r7.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial clause: Gabriel became high, poised at the highest horizon in his real form.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وهو بالأفق الأعلى } جملة في موضع الحال، والمعنى فاستوى عاليا، أي استوى جبريل عاليا على صورته

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r8.claim: Ufuq means a side or region of the sky and its plural is āfāq; the word also varies as ufuq/ufuq.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r8.anchor: والأفق ناحية السماء وجمعه آفاق. وقال قتادة: هو الموضع الذي تأتي منه الشمس. وكذا قال سفيان: هو الموضع الذي تطلع منه الشمس. ونحوه عن مجاهد. ويقال: أفق وأفق مثل عسر وعسر

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r9.speaker: قتادة وسفيان ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r9.claim: Qatāda, Sufyān, and Mujāhid describe the horizon as the place from which the sun comes or rises.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو الموضع الذي تأتي منه الشمس. وكذا قال سفيان: هو الموضع الذي تطلع منه الشمس. ونحوه عن مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r10.claim: A horse called afaq is excellent; a poet’s phrase “an afaq chestnut” illustrates the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r10.anchor: وفرس أفق بالضم أي رائع وكذلك الأنثى قال الشاعر: أرجل لمتي وأجر ذيلي وتحمل شكتي أفق كميت

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r11.claim: The view that “he” is Muḥammad at the highest horizon on the night journey is weak, since the proposed coordination is awkward outside poetic necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r11.anchor: وقيل: «وهو» أي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { بالأفق الأعلى } يعني ليلة الإسراء وهذا ضعيف لأنه يقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r12.claim: The correct reading is Gabriel in his original form: Muḥammad had seen him as a man and wanted to see his true form, so Gabriel filled the eastern horizon.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r12.anchor: والصحيح استوى جبريل عليه السلام وجبريل بالأفق الأعلى على صورته الأصلية لأنه كان يتمثل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل بالوحي في صورة رجل، فأحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يراه على صورته الحقيقية، فاستوى في أفق المشرق فملأ الأفق
